reasons: No tests or sample expected outputs are visible in this file.
Many default values are hardcoded and silently replace missing data, so bad input can look valid.
Colour and CSS content is repeated across the terminal, Markdown and master-file formatters, so edits must be made in several places.
Force overwrite of MASTER.md has no backup.
Dial input is converted with a plain integer conversion, so bad text fails without a helpful message.

terms.meaning: a plain text table where each row is a record and columns are separated by commas; the design data is stored this way.
the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, a standard that sets readability rules such as minimum text contrast.
a 0 to 1 score of how bright a colour looks to the eye, used here to tell dark backgrounds from light ones.
a colour written as a hash sign followed by six letters or digits, such as a web colour code.
hidden control characters that make terminal text coloured or bold; they take up no visible space.
a plain text format that uses simple symbols for headings, lists and tables, and is shown as formatted text by many tools.
a named value in a web stylesheet, such as a colour name, that can be reused across the design.
a cleaned, safe version of a name that uses only lowercase letters, digits, dashes and underscores so it can be used as a folder name.
a trick where a name like dot-dot slash lets a program write files outside the folder it should use.
a 1 to 10 setting that nudges design choices toward calm or bold, still or animated, or spacious or dense.
a JavaScript animation library; the motion snippets are sample code written for it.

sections.name: _generate_intelligent_overrides (part 1)
sections.title: Builds page-specific design guidance from searches
sections.what: Searches the style, UX and landing guidance data for a page description and turns the best matches into layout, color and recommendation notes for that page. If nothing is found, it returns a simple default layout and points the reader back to the master design rules.
sections.why: Lets each page get its own hints without a hardcoded list of page types. The searches are the main source of guidance.
sections.watch_out: Some UX 'Don't' text is stored in the components list under an 'Avoid' label, so that list means advice to avoid rather than real components.

sections.name: _generate_intelligent_overrides (part 2)
sections.title: Adds UX, landing and fallback guidance
sections.what: Adds UX do and don't advice into the recommendations and avoid lists, adds the landing page section order and call-to-action placement, and sets fallback guidance when the searches return nothing useful. It also supplies a generic recommendation pointing to the master rules when there is no advice at all.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The unique_components field is always returned empty, so anything expecting it to hold data will see nothing.

sections.name: _detect_page_type
sections.title: Guesses the page type from keywords
sections.what: Looks for keywords in the page description, such as dashboard, checkout or pricing, and returns the first matching page type. If no keyword matches, it looks at the style search results before falling back to a general type.
sections.why: Gives each page a readable type label that other parts of the design output can use.
sections.watch_out: Matching is by substring and the first match wins, so a short word like post can match unrelated words and an earlier category can hide a later one.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Command line runner for design system
sections.what: When the file is run directly, it reads a search phrase, an optional project name and an output format, builds the design system, and prints the text. It does not expose the save or dial options that the search tool offers.
sections.why: Gives a quick way to preview a design system from the terminal.
sections.watch_out: Only the project name and format are accepted here, so anyone expecting the save options must use the search tool instead.

summary: Builds a complete design guide for a project (colours, fonts, layout, motion, spacing and rules) from the CSV data and outputs it as terminal text, Markdown, or project files.
purpose: Gives the owner a consistent starting design from a short product description, so visual choices come from one place instead of being made ad hoc.
why: The code states several reasons: separate searches are combined so colours agree with the chosen style; existing design files are protected from being overwritten; folder names are cleaned to stop path tricks. Likely reason for the dials: simple 1 to 10 controls for common design choices.
how: 1. Read the optional dial values and convert them to tiers. 2. Find the product category from the query. 3. Look up the matching reasoning rule. 4. Search the style, colour, typography and landing areas, adding dial-based style hints. 5. Pick the style, colour mode, palette, font and layout. 6. If the motion dial is set, pick a motion snippet. 7. Assemble one design record. 8. Format it as terminal text or Markdown. 9. Optionally write MASTER.md and a page file into a design-system folder.
inputs: A short product description; an optional project name; output format ascii or markdown; optional dial values from 1 to 10 for variance, motion and density; optional page name; optional output folder; optional force flag.
outputs: A dictionary with the formatted text, the raw design record, and a save-result dictionary. When persist is on, files are written under design-system/<project>/ as MASTER.md and optionally pages/<page>.md.
risks: Force mode overwrites MASTER.md with no backup, which can erase earlier hand edits. Many fallback values such as default colours and font names silently replace missing data. Files are written before the text is formatted, so a later error can leave files behind. Non-numeric dial values raise an error.
debug: If the style or colours look wrong, check the query words and which area was detected, then open the matching row in the data files. If no files appear, read the persistence status: skipped_exists means MASTER.md already exists and force is needed. If terminal colour blocks look wrong, check the COLORTERM setting and the encoding. If a dial error appears, confirm the dial value is a whole number. Try a plain query without dials to narrow the cause.
